items.headline: The comeback flips it — USA storms back to win the Presidents Cup
items.body: The upset that looked all but locked never happened. Trailing the Internationals 10.5-7.5 heading into Sunday's singles at Medinah, Team USA roared back — grabbing 9.5 of a possible 12 points to win 17-13, the biggest final-day comeback in Presidents Cup history. Rookie Jackson Koivun was a revelation, Scottie Scheffler led the team in points, and Jacob Bridgeman rolled in the clinching par putt. It's an 11th straight U.S. win, but for two days the world team had them genuinely sweating.
items.say: Remember that golf event outside Chicago where the international team was about to pull off a historic upset? Team USA came all the way back on the last day to win it — biggest final-day comeback the event's ever had. Total heartbreak for the underdogs. You catch any of it?

items.headline: Football in a soccer temple — Ravens walk off the Cowboys in Rio
items.body: The NFL's first-ever game in Rio de Janeiro delivered a heart-stopper. With seven seconds left inside the legendary Maracanã, Lamar Jackson hit Zay Flowers for 27 yards and kicker Tyler Loop drilled a 56-yarder as time expired to beat Dallas 34-31 — sweet redemption for the second-year kicker after a miss ended Baltimore's season last winter. A gridiron game in Brazil's most famous soccer cathedral, decided at the buzzer.
items.say: Did you see the NFL played its first game ever in Rio, inside that giant famous soccer stadium? The Ravens won it on a 56-yard field goal as time ran out. Football in a soccer temple, walk-off finish — pretty wild. You a Cowboys guy, or just here for the vibes?

items.headline: The bracket's set — and a losing team is going to the playoffs as a division champ
items.body: Baseball's regular season wrapped, and the field is locked: Wild Card Series all start Tuesday. The quirk everyone's talking about — the Astros won the AL West at 79-81, becoming the first team ever to win a division with a losing record in a full 162-game season. The Phillies snuck in as the last NL wild card, and the Rays (who clinched the AL East at Yankee Stadium) grabbed the top overall seed. October's here.
items.say: The baseball playoffs are set and start Tuesday — and get this, one of the division winners actually had a losing record, first time that's ever happened over a full season. Only in baseball. You got a team still alive?

items.headline: Madonna's back, Taylor makes history — the VMAs delivered
items.body: MTV's Video Music Awards went off last night with Snoop Dogg hosting. Madonna opened the show with her first VMA performance in 23 years — joined by Sabrina Carpenter and Charli xcx — and walked away the night's biggest winner with seven moonmen, including Artist of the Year. Taylor Swift took Video of the Year for 'The Fate of Ophelia' and passed Beyoncé to become the most-awarded artist in VMA history. There was even a Kacey Musgraves tribute to Dolly Parton and a Video Vanguard nod for Nirvana.
items.say: The VMAs were on last night — Madonna performed for the first time in like 23 years and cleaned up, and Taylor Swift is now the most-awarded artist in the show's history. Always a fun mess of a night. You watch the whole thing, or just catch the clips after?

items.headline: Florida stuns No. 4 Ole Miss — and it wasn't close
items.body: The Swamp threw a party Saturday. Florida rolled fourth-ranked Ole Miss 52-28, with Jadan Baugh running for three touchdowns and the Gators never letting the Rebels get within a single score late. Florida jumped into the top 10 in the new rankings, and it's one more banana-peel Saturday in a college season full of them. (No. 1 Texas, meanwhile, hung on again.)
items.say: Florida just blew out Ole Miss, who were ranked fourth — 52 to 28, wasn't even close. College football's been so chaotic this year, somebody big loses every weekend. You following anybody this season?

items.headline: Hockey's back tomorrow — champs raise the banner, a phenom debuts
items.body: The NHL drops the puck on a new season Tuesday night with an ESPN tripleheader. The Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes raise their banner against Florida, the Rangers visit Boston, and Chicago plays at Vegas. Up in Canada, 18-year-old No. 1 pick Gavin McKenna is expected to make his NHL debut for Toronto against Montreal. It kicks off the league's first 84-game season in more than 30 years.
items.say: Hockey season starts tomorrow — the Hurricanes raise their championship banner, and there's a big rookie phenom, Gavin McKenna, making his debut. Opening night's always got a good buzz. You follow the NHL at all, or is it a spring thing for you?

items.headline: Silent Hill goes to Scotland — and it's genuinely scary again
items.body: For the gamers (and horror fans): 'Silent Hill: Townfall' just dropped, and it's the first game in the long-running series told fully in first person. Made by Scottish studio Screen Burn and set in a fog-drowned fictional Scottish town in 1996, it's earning strong reviews for nailing that dread-soaked, dreamlike Silent Hill mood. Reviewers say it plays more like a creepy interactive movie than a jump-scare fest.
items.say: That horror game series Silent Hill just put out a new one, and it's set in this eerie little Scottish town — supposed to be properly unsettling. Perfect spooky-season stuff. You play any games, or is that not your world?

items.headline: Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson bring 'Verity' to theaters Friday
items.body: A big grown-up thriller lands this weekend: 'Verity,' opening Friday (Oct. 2), adapts Colleen Hoover's twisty bestseller with Dakota Johnson as a struggling writer hired to finish an injured author's book series — only to stumble on a disturbing hidden manuscript. Anne Hathaway plays the mysterious author, with Josh Hartnett rounding out the cast. It's the kind of tense, is-she-lying page-turner that's built for date night.
items.say: There's a new thriller out Friday called 'Verity,' with Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson — based on that Colleen Hoover book everyone was reading. Looks properly twisty. You into the tense psychological ones, or more of a popcorn person?

items.headline: Slipknot go big — a 2027 stadium tour just got announced
items.body: The masked metal icons are going stadium-sized: Slipknot announced their '(sic)est Stadium Tour' for summer 2027, throwing fan events at London's Wembley Stadium and LA's SoFi Stadium today to kick off the reveal and give fans first crack at tickets. It's a huge swing for a band that built its name in sweaty clubs — and a good excuse to revisit the video that made them famous.
items.say: Slipknot just announced a big stadium tour for next summer — the masked metal band, if you're not familiar. Wild to think they're playing football stadiums now. That 'Duality' video was everywhere back in the day. You have a genre you always come back to?
